Organizar o discurso com conectores de c: Organise what you say with connectors of contrast and concession («pero, sino, sin embargo, aunque, a pesar de que»), of cause and consequence («como, ya que, por eso, así que, de modo que») and of addition, order, time and condition («además, en primer lugar, en cuanto, siempre que»), choosing the right mood (indicative or subjunctive) when the connector requires it.
Você liga ideias com conectores variados: You can link ideas with a range of connectors, which makes what you say and write clearer and more natural. Next lesson: opinions and debate, where these connectors are very useful.
Diga cinco frases com «pero», «porque» e: Say five sentences with «pero», «porque» and «y». Then say two hypotheses with «si» (one possible and one unreal) to review the mood after «si».
PASSO 1: «pero» liga duas ideias que se: STEP 1: «pero» joins two contrasting ideas, like English "but": «Es caro, pero es bueno». STEP 2: English "but" has a second job that Spanish gives to another word. After a NEGATIVE, when you correct and replace ("not X but Y"), Spanish uses «sino»: «No es rojo, sino azul» (It's not red but blue). If a verb follows, use «sino que»: «No lo compró, sino que lo alquiló» (He didn't buy it — he rented it). Don't confuse it with «si no» (if not), two words. STEP 3: «sin embargo» and «no obstante» are more formal than «pero», like English "however": «Es caro. Sin embargo, vale la pena». STEP 4: «en cambio» and «mientras que» contrast two situations, English "whereas", "on the other hand": «Yo estudio por la mañana; mi hermano, en cambio, estudia por la noche», «Aquí llueve mucho, mientras que allí hace sol». STEP 5: «aunque» covers two English words. With the indicative, it's a known fact, English "although": «Aunque llueve, salimos» (Although it's raining, we're going out). With the subjunctive, it's hypothetical or doesn't matter, English "even if": «Aunque llueva, saldremos» (Even if it rains, we'll go out). STEP 6: «a pesar de» (despite, in spite of) comes with a noun or an infinitive: «A pesar del frío», «A pesar de estar cansado» (despite being tired — infinitive, not gerund). «A pesar de que» (despite the fact that) comes with a conjugated verb, usually indicative: «A pesar de que estaba cansado, vino». STEP 7: «por más que» and «por mucho que» express useless effort, English "however much", with the subjunctive: «Por más que lo intente, no lo consigo», «Por mucho que estudie, no lo recuerdo». STEP 8: «aun cuando» is a more formal alternative to «aunque» and also takes both moods.

PASSO 1: para dar a causa de algo, use «: STEP 1: to give the cause, use «porque» (because), which answers «¿por qué?»: «No fui porque estaba enfermo». STEP 2: English "as" and "since" can give a cause in the middle of a sentence ("I didn't go as I was ill"); Spanish «como» only gives a cause at the START: «Como estaba enfermo, no fui» (As I was ill, I didn't go). «No fui como estaba enfermo» is wrong — in the middle, use «porque» or «ya que». STEP 3: English "since" (causal) is «ya que» or «puesto que» — not «desde», which is only "since" for time: «Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame» (Since you're here, help me). «Dado que» is similar and more formal. STEP 4: «debido a» (due to, owing to) and «a causa de» (because of) take a noun: «debido a la lluvia», «a causa del frío». With a verb, use «debido a que». STEP 5: «gracias a» is a positive cause («Gracias a ti, aprobé»); «por culpa de» is a negative one (because of, it's … 's fault): «Por culpa del tráfico, llegué tarde». STEP 6: for consequence, use «por eso», «así que», «por lo tanto» and «por consiguiente». English "so" is the big trap: "so" meaning "therefore" is «así que» or «por eso» («Estaba enfermo, así que no fui»), while "so" meaning "very" is «tan» («tan cansado»). Never «tan» for "therefore". STEP 7: «por lo tanto» and «por consiguiente» are formal, English "therefore", "consequently", usually followed by a comma: «Por lo tanto, no podemos aceptar». STEP 8: «tan… que» and «tanto… que» show intensity and consequence, English "so … that": «Estaba tan cansado que se durmió», «Trabajó tanto que se enfermó». STEP 9: «de modo que» has two uses. With the indicative it's a consequence: «Llegó tarde, de modo que perdió el tren». With the subjunctive it's a purpose: «Habla alto, de modo que todos te oigan».

PASSO 1: para acrescentar uma ideia, use: STEP 1: to add an idea, use «además» (besides, what's more), «también», «asimismo» (more formal, "likewise") and «incluso» (even). «Es barato y, además, está cerca.» STEP 2: to order your ideas, use «en primer lugar», «en segundo lugar», «por último», and «por una parte… por otra parte…» (on the one hand… on the other). To conclude, use «en resumen», «en definitiva», «en conclusión». STEP 3: time connectors like «cuando», «en cuanto», «tan pronto como» and «después de que» take the indicative for habits or the past, and the subjunctive for what's still to come (lesson 44): «Cuando llego, cenamos» (habit), «Cuando llegue, cenaremos» (future). STEP 4: «hasta que» follows the same logic: «Esperé hasta que llegó» (past), «Esperaré hasta que llegue» (future). STEP 5: «antes de que» always takes the subjunctive. STEP 6: condition connectors like «siempre que», «con tal de que», «a menos que» and «salvo que» (unless) take the subjunctive: «Iré siempre que tenga tiempo», «No iremos a menos que nos inviten». STEP 7: «mientras» meaning "while" (at the same time) takes the indicative; meaning "as long as" it takes the subjunctive: «Mientras estudio, escucho música», «Mientras no llueva, saldremos».
o português usa o futuro do subjuntivo d: Remember lesson 44: English "When I arrive" and "until he comes" use the present; Spanish uses the present subjunctive for the future («Cuando llegue», «hasta que llegue») and never the future («cuando llegaré»). The same goes for «en cuanto», «mientras» (as long as) and «siempre que» (provided that).

Marta e Andrés conversam sobre um convit: Marta and Andrés talk about a job offer in another city and use connectors to weigh up the pros and cons.
— Você já decidiu se aceita o trabalho e: — Have you decided whether to take the job in Valencia?
— Ainda não. Em primeiro lugar, o salári: — Not yet. Firstly, the salary is better and, what's more, the company offers flexible hours.
— Que não conheço ninguém lá. Embora eu: — That I don't know anyone there. Even though I have a cousin in Alicante, it's not the same. And on the other hand, I really like my flat here.
— Pois é, mas seu apartamento é pequeno,: — True, but your flat is small, whereas there you could rent one with a terrace.
— É verdade. No entanto, não quero decid: — That's true. However, I don't want to rush the decision. However much I think about it, I can't make up my mind.
— Então peça alguns dias de prazo, para: — Then ask for a few days so you can decide calmly.
— Boa ideia. Assim que terminar a reuniã: — Good idea. As soon as today's meeting is over, I'll write to my boss. That's why I'm telling you first.
— Apesar de tudo, no seu lugar eu iria,: — In spite of everything, if I were you I'd go, as long as you could come back often.
